value.title: Coder packet — ddocs adapter — edges, schema facts, derived state, degradation (008-ddocs-scan)

sections.name: mission
sections.value:
You build ONE unit of plan 008-ddocs-scan: **ddocs adapter — edges, schema facts, derived state, degradation** — Everything about ddocs that needs the world: resolve schemas, fetch the corpus edge graph, compute gate-terminal and derived state, stamp the dd version, and degrade honestly when the binary is absent. Pure parsing lives in core; only the process spawn lives in the daemon.

WHY THIS PLAN EXISTS, so you can spot a dead premise rather than implement one: flowspace3 cannot see deterministic documents today. A `*.dd.json` is classified as a config format and skipped by discovery (crates/parsers/src/discovery.rs:720), while its GENERATED `*.dd.md` sibling IS indexed as a flat heading tree — so the only ddoc content in the index is a lossy projection that can be arbitrarily stale with nothing in the file saying so. We make the ROW the chunk, keyed on (file, section, id), cited with dd's own address so a hit pastes straight into `ddocs get`.

You build this behind the interface below so the PM can compose it without reading your internals. You report to the PM (pij-driving-nigel), not to prime, not to Jordan.

Report EVERY flowspace3 miss (a search that returned nothing where you expected matches, a confusing envelope, a bad next_action) to the PM immediately AND with `harness observe`. Day-one agent feedback IS this product's test suite. CAPTURE freely; NEVER clear the observation buffer — the drain is o-prime-owned and clearing destroys other seats' live observations.

value.text: Orient: read your unit's row in the impl-guide (impl-guide.dd.json), the plan phase/tasks you own, and the interface contract. Run `harness boot --json` in your worktree before changing anything. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: `flowspace3 search "<question>"` for every meaning-shaped question before grep (exact identifiers may still grep); report every miss or confusing envelope as friction.
Ack FIRST: reply to the PM with your read of the unit + a numbered implementation plan before writing code. Corrections to the packet are welcome — bring evidence.

Implement using the /builder implement discipline: work the tasks in order, keep the execution log honest, tests alongside code — your unit's test suite must prove the interface contract without the other units present.
Stay inside your unit's paths (scope below). If the work forces you outside them, STOP and ask the PM — that is a composition concern, not yours to solve unilaterally.
Commit with `harness commit` (conventional commits are binding), status card at start and end of each unit of work (`pij report now`).
Done = `harness checks` green in YOUR worktree + your unit's tests proving the contract. Report done to the PM with the evidence, then hold for composition questions — do not merge anything.
Capture friction with `harness observe` the moment it bites; list, never clear the buffer.

DOGFOOD VIA THE CLI, NOT MCP. `flowspace3 search "<question>"` from a shell works; the flowspace3 MCP tools are NOT reachable from a subagent/worker context (o-prime backlog row 40, and four scouts hit it today). Exact identifiers may still grep. Also: `flowspace3 ask` on PROD currently answers from a FAKE provider (DL-059, disclosed in-envelope) — search/get/tree are real, so never report an `ask` answer as evidence.

RUN `--help` ON A VERB BEFORE YOU USE IT. This is a standing habit here, not a suggestion — it is how the pij send body hazard was found. Relatedly: NEVER compose a pij message body inside double quotes; backticks and $( ) are eaten by YOUR shell before pij runs and the command has already executed. Write the body to a file and use `pij send <peer> --body-file <path>`.

TOOLCHAIN IS PINNED AND YOU MAY NOT CHANGE IT: cargo 1.95.0 · ddocs 0.1.0 (node 24.7.0). All four units read ONE installed toolchain, so a unit upgrading it invalidates its siblings retroactively and INVISIBLY — they stay green and become wrong. Your done report MUST repeat the versions you actually observed (`cargo --version`, `ddocs --json version`), not the ones written here.

TEST DATABASE: do NOT run `docker compose up -d` — a shared `flowspace3-db` container is already healthy on port 5433 and belongs to no one seat. Do not remove, rename or restart it. Create your OWN database on that stack and point FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL at it, e.g. `docker exec flowspace3-db psql -U flowspace3 -d flowspace3 -c 'CREATE DATABASE <your_unit>_test'` then `export FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://flowspace3:flowspace3@127.0.0.1:5433/<your_unit>_test`. `harness checks` refuses to guess a database on purpose — on 2026-08-27 guessing migrated a production one.

MUTATION-CHECK EVERY TEST YOU ARE TOLD TO WRITE: break the code, watch that NAMED test fail, restore it, watch it pass. A test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence. Say in your done report which tests you mutation-checked and what mutation you used.

FILL THE CONTRACT, NEVER WIDEN IT (tenet 2). The wave-0 types in crates/core/src/ddoc.rs and crates/core/src/element.rs are FROZEN at commit f13186b. If your unit needs one of them changed, that is a PM ruling — stop and ask with the reason. Do not edit crates/core/src/ddoc.rs or element.rs yourself.

THE `ddocs --json derive` VERB IS BEING BUILT BY dd RIGHT NOW and you must NOT wait for it, code against it, or feature-flag it. Use `fs3_core::ddoc::derive_state` — the single frozen wave-0 function — exactly as your contract says. Context so you understand why it is one function: dd's own deriveItems/deriveState/deriveRollup are unreachable from both Node and the CLI, so flowspace3 must implement the rule itself, which is the drifting second implementation dd explicitly warned against. We have committed to consuming their verb and DELETING our implementation in the same commit the day it ships. Keeping the rule behind one function is what makes that a one-line change — so do not inline the logic, do not duplicate it, and do not 'optimise' it into a call site.

ISOLATION — a defect that cost your sibling 20 minutes today and is invisible when it happens. The `edit` tool resolves a RELATIVE section header against the SESSION ROOT, which is fixed at spawn and NOT changed by `cd`. Pass ABSOLUTE paths rooted at your own worktree in every edit section header and every write path, always. Never open any absolute path containing another tree's name — everything you need is committed on your own branch at the same relative paths. If an absolute header is ever rejected, STOP and tell the PM; do not fall back to relative. (Verified by the PM: absolute headers are accepted and apply correctly.)
The PM is your interface: acks, questions, done reports. You never message prime or Jordan directly unless the PM's seat is dead.
DEFER to the PM: interface changes (they affect sibling units), dependency additions, schema/migration changes, anything outside your paths.
Your evidence outranks the packet: if the brief is wrong, say so at ack or stop-and-ask with the measurement — do not silently code around it.

value.forbidden_note:
Never touch another unit's paths, .harness/government/**, the plan's flow state, or crates/core/src/ddoc.rs and crates/core/src/element.rs (the wave-0 frozen contract). Never merge and never open a PR — the PM composes. Never remove/rename/restart the shared flowspace3-db container.

LINE-LEVEL COLLISION MAP (wave 2): ONE LINE, SHARED WITH u4: the module list in crates/daemon/src/lib.rs, where you add `pub mod ddoc;` and u4 adds nothing (u4 edits existing daemon modules only). You also add one job-kind string constant to runner::KINDS. Both are trivial-merge points. NOTE: u4 edits crates/daemon/src/search.rs, read.rs and http.rs — you must not. You own every subprocess call in this plan; u4 owns every wire type.

value.text: Unit implements the interface contract in the impl-guide row, verbatim or with PM-ruled amendments.
Unit test suite passes standalone and proves the contract.
harness checks green in your worktree.

The SNAP-IN RECIPE shipped with the unit (tenet 4): the exact wiring the composer will paste — config shape, construction call, registration line — as a doc comment or section in your unit's service page. You never wire it in yourself.
Done report to PM: what shipped, evidence, deviations, anything the composer must know.

Your unit's REQUIRED test cases from the impl-guide row all exist and are mutation-checked. Named explicitly so acceptance is mechanical, not a judgement call: (a) each `parse_*` over a real recorded envelope; (b) a recorded `graph` envelope containing `kind: "file"` edges — which dd main CANNOT yet emit, since PR #12 is open — proving the inverse index is built to receive them; (c) a recorded `graph` envelope with NO `kind` field on its edges — the shape dd main actually emits today — parsing cleanly with every edge defaulted to `"document"`; (c2) an unknown rel surviving `edges_for` unfiltered; (d) a `pressure` edge whose target is the literal `not-applicable`, asserted NOT to become a dangling edge, and asserted to be keyed on the rel rather than the field name; (e) `probe` against a binary path that does not exist returning `DdocTooling::absent()` with no Err, and the scan path still producing rows — the degradation proof; (f) a `degraded` envelope and an `ok`-with-empty-issues envelope, asserting health is NOT inferred from the latter; (g) `derive_state` disagreeing with a row's stored `state`, asserting the derived value wins.

Your done report names the OBSERVED cargo and ddocs versions, the mutations you used to check your tests, and — explicitly — what you ASSUMED about the composition you do not own (call order, key scoping, pre-existing store state, who runs first on a cold index). A unit can be green and mutation-checked and still carry a baked-in assumption that only surfaces at the seams; volunteering it beats the PM discovering it while wiring.
